transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-11
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Martinez (Redwood SE), Monica Ruiz (Atlas - Dir ML), Devon Lee (Atlas - Platform), Priya Nair (Atlas - Security), Liam O'Hara (Atlas - Product)
Notes/links: onboarding runbook (placeholder) https://redwood.app/drive/poc-setup-deck , initial benchmark sheet link to be shared in follow-up

Summary: quick check on access, dev env readiness for POC, and who is blocked on what. Reviewed initial latency/cost approach (dedicated pool vs hosted fallbacks) and security gating items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, it's Sofia and Ethan from Redwood, thanks for carving time today
[00:18] Monica: hey -- thanks, good to see you, we have a quick update from our side on infra access
[00:30] Ethan: hi all, i'll be driving the bench and the env setup, quick agenda: 1) access, 2) env readiness, 3) bench plan, 4) security items and next steps
[01:05] Devon: right now we've got the service account created, but devs don't yet have VPC peering, we have a ticket open with infra, trying to get CIDR details
[01:22] Sofia: ok cool, do you have the subnet CIDRs and a contact we can coordinate with?
[01:35] Devon: yeah i'll drop them in chat after, but we do need the exact IP ranges the redwood side needs to allow, and also the SG rules
[02:10] Priya: also from security we need to confirm encryption in transit and that KMS is used for keys, is that supported in the private deployment?
[02:24] Ethan: yes we support KMS integrations, there's a small config for the key alias, and we can run HSM if needed in the private on-prem flow, though that is more advanced
[02:45] Monica: timeline wise we are trying to get POC results in 3 weeks, is that still feasible if infra peering slips a bit?
[03:02] Sofia: we can do a hybrid approach: start hosted for initial functional tests, then fail over to dedicated/private once peering is ready. it will change cost/latency numbers though
[03:28] Monica: understood, that might work but we need the baseline numbers on dedicated to compare
[03:45] Ethan: plan for bench: run a 1k request sample with avg seq lengths of 128 and 512, test on quantized model variant and full float baseline. we'll collect p50/p95 latency and token cost.
[04:05] Devon: do you need any agent on our side to run the samples or you will call our endpoints?
[04:18] Ethan: we'll run from Redwood's test harness against the provisioned endpoint; if peering is delayed we can run from hosted endpoints to mimic latency, but that won't reflect private network latencies
[04:52] Liam: small Q on model versions - can we pin to a specific model and quantization profile for the POC? we don't want auto-rolls to change results mid-test
[05:07] Sofia: absolutely, we'll pin to model v1.2-quant-sm and lock rollouts; we'll document the exact model hash in the runbook
[05:35] Monica: about data retention, we need to ensure logs from the POC are either not stored or stored only in our tenant for compliance
[05:52] Ethan: by default hosted logs are retained but we can configure no-persist for PII workloads; dedicated/private gives you explicit control — we'll include retention config in runbook
[06:15] Priya: do you have SOC2 or a security questionnaire we can start with?
[06:27] Sofia: yes we'll share SOC2 summary and our security packet; for the deep dive we can bring Redwood security to that meeting
[07:05] Monica: can you also share a smaller checklist for VPN and SAML so our infra can move faster?
[07:18] Sofia: yes that's part of the onboarding runbook we'll send after this call (Sofia: note)
[07:34] Devon: quick bit on routing: our infra team would prefer keeping traffic internal, do you support VPC peering and private link style connections?
[07:48] Ethan: we support VPC peering and private endpoints; depending on the deployment we can do VPC peering for dedicated or a private link for hosted private connectivity
[08:12] Monica: any gotchas we should expect with the KV cache when moving to shorter seq lengths? we've seen some weird cache misses in other vendors
[08:30] Ethan: good Q - our runtime uses prefix and KV caching; for short seqs the overhead is usually lower but depending on prompt patterns you might see cache churn. we'll include recommended batch sizes and cache TTL in the runbook
[09:05] Monica: perfect. can you run the first bench with the quantized variant so we can see cost delta?
[09:16] Ethan: yes we'll do quantized first then float baseline. expected delta often 2-4x in token cost depending on throughput
[09:28] Sophia: [sic] note: speaker mis-attribution, Sofia clarified in chat that she meant "Sofia" not "Sophia"
[09:40] Priya: on key management, our org uses AWS KMS, we need integration details and assurance on key rotation
[09:54] Ethan: we support AWS KMS, you can supply CMK ARN and we will use it for encrypting persistent caches and keys; rotation is handled by AWS side, we advise periodic rotation and will accept new aliases
[10:20] Monica: ok good. about monitoring, can we get per-route latency logs and token usage per API key?
[10:32] Sofia: yes console exposes per-route metrics, token breakdowns and you can supply different API keys per team. we can also send a sample dashboard link
[11:02] Devon: small ask: our infra requires IP allowlist, can you provide the egress IPs for the test harness?
[11:18] Ethan: we'll provide a short list of egress ranges for the timeframe of the test in the runbook
[11:48] Monica: let's talk about success criteria: we want p95 <= 350ms for 128 seq on dedicated and total token cost under $0.0008 per token equivalent for the POC to consider extending to Dedicated purchase
[12:05] Sofia: noted, we'll calibrate bench to those SLOs and report back; if we can't hit them we will suggest tuning knobs (batching, quant profiles, smaller model variants)
[12:28] Monica: any regulatory issues with EU data residency — some customers require EU-only, do you support region pinning?
[12:40] Ethan: yes we can pin region for hosted and dedicated allocations, private on-prem is fully local; we'll surface region options in runbook
[13:05] Liam: client question: how do rollouts and canaries work, we want deterministic behavior during POC, no automatic fallbacks that would change model behavior mid-test
[13:22] Sofia: you can pin model versions and disable automatic fallback for the POC; we usually recommend a canary for production, but for POC we can keep static mapping
[13:45] Devon: from our side, next blockers are VPC peering and the egress IPs; we'll prioritize those two tickets
[14:00] Monica: anything else on infra?
[14:07] Devon: no that's it
[14:15] Sofia: quick recap of remaining items: runbook, egress IPs, CIDRs, sample prompts, bench run and security deep dive, agreed?
[14:28] Monica: yes
[14:32] Ethan: timeline recap — we will run an initial bench by 2025-02-17 and share results; runbook and egress details by 2025-02-14; security deep dive week of 2025-02-24
[14:55] Priya: noted, i'll prepare our security questionnaire and send a prioritized list of must-haves for the POC
[15:10] Sofia: great, i'll attach the runbook and SOC2 summary in follow-up and mark action owners in CRM
[15:28] Monica: thanks everyone
[15:35] Liam: thanks, bye

End of transcript.

Artifacts referenced: onboarding runbook (will be shared) https://redwood.app/drive/poc-setup-deck ; benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared) placeholder: https://redwood.app/drive/atlas-bench-2025

- Redwood: send onboarding runbook + VPN/SAML checklist + egress IP list (Sofia) by 2025-02-14
- Redwood SE: run quantized + float benches and upload spreadsheet (Ethan) by 2025-02-17
- Atlas: provide sample prompts, traffic profile, and CIDRs (Monica/Devon) by 2025-02-18
- Security deep dive scheduled for week of 2025-02-24 (TBD exact slot)
